executive_assessment.text: The 2024 South assessment identifies interacting service, governance and climate vulnerabilities in Sebha, Murzuq, Ghat, Kufra and Ubari; local conflict and adaptation shortfalls are not causally equated.
Historical flood exposure and 2025 water-system outputs add named-place detail. July 2026 cereal estimates remain forecasts, not final harvest results.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-07-16 reports: FAO reports dry October-November 2025 weather delayed planting and reduced area; March 2026 rainfall improved some regions but remained well below average in cereal-producing Al Jabal al Akhdar.

FAO's official summary of its rapid geospatial assessment reports 36,245 flooded hectares in Benghazi following the September 2023 eastern Libya disaster. This is mapped flood exposure, not a ranking of fatalities or total human impacts.

Source dated 2025-01-19 reports: The UN names Sebha, Murzuq, Ghat, Kufra and Ubari among municipalities facing heat, water scarcity and drought, alongside service deficits, conflict and weak governance; women, youth and displaced people face disproportionate service gaps.

Source dated 2025-01-19 reports: The assessment says unresolved conflicts in Murzuq and Kufra eroded cohesion and stalled reconciliation; climate adaptation and disaster-risk efforts are fragmented and underfunded, leaving communities vulnerable.

The UN 2025 results report describes solar panels under WFP's Hayat project and a water-food nexus programme in Ubari, Ghat, Tahala and Alberkit: four desalination units and ten solar-powered extraction systems reportedly benefited more than 150,000 people.

Source dated 2026-05-03 reports: The report states restored wells provided water access to 75 percent of Qatroun's population, while a Yefren integrated water-resource plan delivered long-distance water to 49,000 residents, 52 percent of them women.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 32 of 33 evidence records and 8 of 8 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

Climate-projection gap: Accessible Libya-specific projections do not provide sufficiently detailed scenario, model-ensemble, spatial and uncertainty information for heat, drought, rainfall, sea level and compound extremes. SIPRI's projections are useful but secondary. (SIPRI)

Attribution gap beyond Storm Daniel: Event attribution is available for the September 2023 rainfall, but comparable Libya-specific attribution evidence for drought trends, groundwater depletion, heat impacts, coastal erosion and agricultural losses was not verified. (World Weather Attribution)
Geographic gap: Derna/eastern Libya is much better documented than many western and southern municipalities. Fezzan water-governance evidence is local and cannot be nationalized.

Population gap: There is insufficient comparable evidence separating impacts by gender, age, disability, income, migrant/refugee status, urban informality and livelihood type. UNICEF and UNHCR identify vulnerable groups, but longitudinal differentiated outcome data are scarce.

Evaluation gap: The 2025 UNDP evaluation provides independent evidence for one climate/energy programme, but the new drought strategy, water-security strategy, local water systems and post-Derna reconstruction lack comparable independent outcome evaluations.

Unintended-effect gap: There is limited systematic evidence on whether climate or reconstruction programmes reinforce territorial inequalities, authority competition, exclusion, maladaptation or unequal resource allocation.

Causal climate-FCV gap: Evidence that climate stress causes violence, recruitment or migration is substantially weaker than evidence that governance, conflict and institutional fragmentation shape vulnerability and response. (SIPRI)
FCV-to-adaptation quantification gap: Qualitative evidence that fragmentation weakens adaptation and recovery is strong, but there is little quantitative estimation of the size of these effects.

Formal climate-reporting gap: The UNFCCC National Communication table contained no listed Libyan submission at the time of verification. UN reporting indicates NDC development has advanced, but this research did not verify a finalized/submitted Libyan NDC. (UNFCCC)

Policy implementation gap: The 2026 drought and water strategies establish intentions and targets; financing, institutional ownership, municipal execution, maintenance and measurable resilience outcomes remain unresolved. (UNDP)

*None are wholly without traceable support. However, coping-capacity and resilience-peace-capacity remain only partially covered because current evidence is dominated by programme outputs and localized qualitative cases rather than independently evaluated household, community or peace outcomes.
The FAO July 2026 cereal harvest and import values are forecasts, not verified final outcomes, and are not attributed to anthropogenic climate change.

Sources describe connected climate, governance and conflict vulnerabilities in southern Libya but do not establish a causal climate-to-violence pathway or show that conflict obstructed a specific adaptation project.
UN annual results describe 2025 water-service outputs; service continuity, distributional reach and independent outcome impacts were not assessed in the accessible passage.
Main independently downloaded both original UN PDFs and inspected the cited pages on 27 October 2026, replacing the intake's indexed-only access limitation for those passages.
The South assessment is a 2024 version synthesizing 2018–2023 assessments. It is not a current October 2026 municipal survey. Its exact January 2025 portal day was not verified from the PDF.
Co-located conflict, governance and climate vulnerabilities do not justify a new causal pathway. National strategies and water installations do not establish durable or equitable outcomes.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
